fix(plugins): a plugin names itself scope-free, so one definition loads alike from a repo and an install (candybar-plugins-vf6g.3gg)

A definition names itself `self` (`.self.data`, `template "self.state"`,
`action "self.go"`, `do: ["self.go", …]`); the loader binds it to the
namespace the plugin loads under, as it binds bare session keys and
refreshes. A plugin spelling its own name under the other scope drops,
naming the `self` form. A config's plugins are the repository's when
discovery found the file at the project or working directory, not by its
name. A placement missing from one scope names the other's spelling.
Unnamed drops answer only within their own scope. Both plugin roots are
refused to every config file's own declarations. Plugin identity is a
typed { scope, name } with one namespace function.

Absorbs candybar-plugins-vf6g.3tv.

fix(daemon): act files that can't be read show as an error, and a restart waits while anything of the act is alive (brandon-unfiled-3248.z676)

Medium review of the update act as a job:
- The act files are read at one edge: a read that throws is an error the
  indicator shows, holds a restart and refuses a click, never a throw out of a
  timer that ends every daemon on the bundle.
- A restart and a second click wait while the act's group is alive, whatever
  its verdict, so a timed-out group still dying, or a child a program left
  behind, holds them as the old in-process child did. An overdue live group is
  ended even when the job's verdict landed first.
- Ending a job whose files are gone is a no-op.
- The reader knows an act by its job, so an act number claimed again names the
  new act.
- The e2e stand-in appends its pid, so a second run fails the test, and ends
  itself after two minutes as well.

fix(daemon): an act's record proves its job by boot and start time, and a reader survives a prune under it (brandon-unfiled-3248.z676)

Review of the update act as a job:
- A reader that lists an act and then finds it pruned by a newer claim looks
  again instead of throwing out of the poll timer and ending the daemon.
- A group seen gone stays gone for that act, so a recycled pid never reads as
  the job again, and an overdue act needs no fresh `ps` to end.
- A record must carry the job's start time, and a job started before this boot
  is never the recorded one; a group the daemon may not signal is someone
  else's. An unfingerprinted job is never started.
- Any throw while claiming withdraws the gated job and its staging.
- An ended act's facts are final and are not read again.

fix(daemon): the update act is a job every daemon reads, so it finishes whatever happens to the daemon that started it (brandon-unfiled-3248.z676)

The act rewrites the bundle the daemon runs from, and as a launch child it
died with its daemon, leaving the bundle torn when the death landed mid-write.
It now runs as a job, a third lifetime beside the waited child and the orphan:
its stdout, stderr and verdict are files it owns, so no pipe leads back to a
dead daemon, and its running is a record keyed by the bundle it writes.

- The record is claimed by renaming a staged act directory to the next act
  number, so one claim wins per bundle whichever socket a daemon serves.
- The job's shell waits on a start gate that opens only once the claim
  stands: a claimer that loses or dies never runs the program.
- A verdict is claimed by link, never overwritten: a deadline cannot replace
  an exit that landed first.
- A second click and the restart's hold read the record at the moment they
  decide; a 2 s clock notices an end, logs it, and restarts on a success.

Done-when, as e2e on the built bundle: SIGKILL the daemon mid-act; the next
daemon shows it running, refuses a second, and restarts on the rebuilt bundle,
or shows the failure it did not start.

fix(colour): the activated segment and its menu plane wear named theme shades; the inter-cell floors go (candybar-joiners-e5r4.dg6)

The segment whose menu is open, the ✕ and blank leads of that menu's rows,
and the plane the rows sit on now select colours the theme names, the way
every closed cell already does. The activated state is the menu hue at a new
`activated` column of the shade table: the hue's muted form on every window
of the ladder, its second lightening on the `muted` position. The plane is
`surface` at every depth. Items are unchanged.

Deleted: the open-trigger colour search and its rays, the plane blend and
its floors, the band item repair at 256 and ansi, every floor stated in
STATE_FLOOR, BAND_FLOORS or SEAM_MIN_DELTA_E, the shortfalls a band carried,
and the `band-floor` render warning with its cases in check and the daemon.
A disclosure no longer carries the ground its row dealt, since nothing reads
it. Text is unchanged: it is still chosen to clear AA on whatever it is
drawn on.

fix(proc): a launch child dies with the process that launched it, SIGKILL included (brandon-unfiled-3248.86ga) (#488)

* fix(proc): a launch child dies with the process that launched it, SIGKILL included (brandon-unfiled-3248.86ga)

A launch child leads its own process group, and everything that ended it
(its timeout, its caller's abort, its own exit) ran inside the launcher.
A daemon that exited left every in-flight group running, reparented to
init for good, and a SIGKILL runs no cleanup to prevent that.

Each launching process now starts one lifeline: an awk program in its
own group, reading a pipe only the launcher holds. Every waited child is
registered on it and deregistered when it settles. When the launcher
ends, however it ends, the kernel closes the pipe, and the lifeline sends
the remaining groups the timeout's own escalation: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL
after the grace. The in-process set of live groups is the truth. A lost
lifeline is logged, and the next launch replaces it and hands it the
whole set.

The binary watch now holds a restart while the update notice's act is
running. That act is a launch child rewriting the bundle the watch
samples, and a restart in the middle would now kill it half-written.

The Pages site's child_process shim gains resident programs, since the
lifeline lives as long as the page's daemon.

* fix(proc): the update act outlives the daemon, and a downed lifeline stands as a warning (brandon-unfiled-3248.86ga)

High review of the lifeline:

- The update act rewrites the bundle, so any daemon exit now killed it
  half-written. A waited launch can say it outlives its launcher, and the
  act does; the binary watch still holds the restart while it runs.
- Why the lifeline is down is one state: the log says each change, and the
  daemon shows it beside the file-events warning, so a broken lifeline
  reaches the bar instead of only daemon.log.
- awk is found on the launcher's PATH, as every launched program is, so a
  machine without /usr/bin/awk (NixOS) is guarded.
- The binary watch says its wait once, through the shared change logger.
- The demo shim's resident programs are programs that answer RESIDENT, one
  registry instead of two.

* fix(proc): the update act dies with the daemon like every child, and a lifeline change redraws every feed (brandon-unfiled-3248.86ga)

Medium review of the lifeline:

- Exempting the update act from the lifeline did not let it outlive the
  daemon: its output pipes lead to the dead daemon, so a shell in it dies of
  SIGPIPE at its next write, and the next daemon has no record of it and
  would start a second. The act is a launch child like any other again; the
  binary watch still holds the restart while it runs.
- The lifeline's seam is an observer of its fault rather than a log. The
  daemon's observer logs each change and wakes every feed, as file events'
  delivery does, so the warning comes and goes on pushed frames too.

* fix(proc): a lifeline's start clears its fault only while it is the current one, and the warning names no daemon (brandon-unfiled-3248.86ga)

Second high review of the lifeline:

- A spawn event from a lifeline already lost no longer clears the fault while
  nothing guards.
- The warning says "their launcher", since bar-pane and the CLI print it too.
- The architecture memory says which children the lifeline holds (those not
  blocking the daemon) and the one window it leaves: a daemon death while the
  update writes the bundle tears it. The durable update act that closes it is
  brandon-unfiled-3248.z676.
